cards.text: Jesus has set out for Jerusalem (Luke 9:51). Now the Lord appoints seventy-two others and sends them ahead of Him to every town and place He's about to visit. SEVENTY-TWO, friend, and back when I lived in the Millers' kitchen I had my mustache full looking after six little cookie cutters!

cards.question: Jesus sends the seventy-two out one at a time, each one on his own.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Before the pairs head out, Jesus gives them a picture: ‘The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.’ Big job, short staff, and every adult with a job just nodded.

cards.question: With a big harvest and only a few workers, what does Jesus tell the seventy-two to do?

answers.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers
Hire more workers from the towns nearby
Let the field rest until next season

cards.question: When Jesus sends them off with ‘Go!’, He tells them He's sending them out like lambs among wolves.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Jesus tells them what to leave behind, and then adds one more thing: do not greet anyone along the road. Friend, I greet every baker at my door like I haven't seen them in ten years, so that one would be HARD for me.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the seventy-two not to carry?

answers.text: A purse or bag or sandals
A staff or cloak or tunic
A lamp or scroll or blanket

cards.text: Whatever house they walk into, Jesus tells them to begin with these words: ‘Peace to this house.’ Not ‘Hey,’ not ‘Nice place,’ but PEACE.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two to say ‘Peace to this house.’ If no man of peace is there, what happens to that peace?

answers.text: It returns to them
It stays on the house anyway
It's lost for good

cards.text: Once they're welcomed into a house, Jesus says eat and drink whatever they're offered, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Whatever's on the table, you eat it, and friend, nobody has EVER had to tell me that twice when there's a warm cookie on it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two to stay at the same house and not move around from house to house.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: When a town welcomes the seventy-two, they eat whatever is set before them. What else does Jesus send them to do there?

answers.text: Heal the sick and tell them God's kingdom is near
Teach the law and settle all their disputes
Gather the people and collect an offering

cards.text: But if a town doesn't welcome them, Jesus tells them to go into the streets and declare something. Not a quiet exit, friend, a STREET announcement.

cards.question: When a town won't welcome the seventy-two, what does Jesus tell them to wipe off as a testimony against it?

answers.text: The dust of the town clinging to their feet
The water of the town's well from their hands
The ashes of the town's fires from their cloaks

cards.text: Friend, I spent years under the dust in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody EVER wiped me off that dramatically. And even then, they still declare, ‘Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
Then Jesus says it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom, the city the LORD rained fire on (Genesis 19:24), than for that town.

cards.question: Jesus says woe to Chorazin and Bethsaida, two towns in Galilee. If the miracles performed in them had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, two cities on the coast, those cities would have ___ long ago.

answers.text: repented
rebelled
rejoiced

cards.text: Jesus says it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for those towns. Then He turns to Capernaum, another town in Galilee: ‘…will you be lifted up to heaven?’

cards.question: Jesus asks Capernaum if it will be lifted up to heaven. What does He say will happen to it instead?

answers.text: It will be brought down to Hades
It will be handed over to its enemies
It will be left in ruins forever

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two that whoever listens to them listens to Him, and whoever rejects them rejects Him. Who else does that person reject?

answers.text: The One who sent Him
The prophets before Him
Moses and the law

cards.text: Mission over, and the seventy-two come back to Jesus with a report. Friend, if those were my bakers, I'd be pacing by the door with my mustache in a knot waiting to hear how it went.

cards.question: What do the seventy-two tell Jesus when they get back?

answers.text: Even the demons submit to them in His name
The dead were raised in every town
Fire fell from heaven at their word

cards.question: The seventy-two come back from their trip discouraged and worn out.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: They come back with joy, and Jesus answers them, ‘I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.’ That's Satan, the devil, and that's not something you hear every day, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two He has given them authority over all the power of the enemy.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Jesus tells them He has given them authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and nothing will harm them. Then He says, ‘Nevertheless,’ and friend, when somebody says nevertheless, the whole conversation is about to turn around.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two not to rejoice that the spirits submit to them. What should they rejoice about instead?

answers.text: That their names are written in heaven
That every town will remember them
That they will see greater miracles

cards.text: At that time Jesus rejoices in the Holy Spirit and declares, ‘I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth…’ Friend, when the Son of God is THIS full of joy, you lean in and you listen.

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned and revealing them to ___.

answers.text: little children
the priests
the rulers

cards.text: Then Jesus says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father.

cards.question: Jesus says no one knows who the Father is except the Son. Who else does He say knows the Father?

answers.text: Those the Son chooses to reveal Him to
Those who study the law most closely
Those who keep every single commandment

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to the disciples and says privately, ‘Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.’ Just them, friend, a FRONT-ROW seat.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that many people wanted to see what they see and hear what they hear, but never did. Who?

answers.text: Many prophets and kings
Many priests and scribes
Many judges and elders
